title: Finite-clopen assembly of the inverse of a smooth dualizing object of varying dimension
statement:
Fix the purity coefficient datum [def-pur-conventions]: $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, a prime $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}(k)$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ inside $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, its valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and $A_{E,j}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^j$ for $j\geq1$. Work on the small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], with the derived operations [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom] and finite-Tor constructible categories [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude]. For a scheme $T$, the coefficient unit $\Lambda_T$ is $(A_{E,n})_T[0]$ at $\Lambda=A_{E,n}$, $n\geq1$, the completed sheaf $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,T}[0]$ at $\Lambda=\mathcal O_E$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients], and its rationalized or common-stage image at $\Lambda=E,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$.

Let $g:V\to B$ be a smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], separated finite-type morphism [def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-finite-type-morphism] between finite-type $k$-schemes. No section and no constant relative dimension are assumed. For $d\geq0$ let $V_d$ be the locus of points $x\in V$ for which $\dim_x(V_{g(x)})=d$, and let $I=\{d:V_d\ne\varnothing\}$. Then $I$ is finite and the $V_d$ are pairwise disjoint open and closed subschemes covering $V$. Each restricted morphism $g_d:V_d\to B$ is smooth separated of finite type and pure relative dimension $d$.

For every $\Lambda\in\{A_{E,n},\mathcal O_E,E,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell\}$ put $\omega_g=Rg^!\Lambda_B$ and $\omega_{g_d}=R(g_d)^!\Lambda_B$, using the constructible exceptional inverse image [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image]. If $j_d:V_d\hookrightarrow V$ is the inclusion, there are derived isomorphisms $Lj_d^*\omega_g\simeq\omega_{g_d}$. At the integral stage these are induced by comparisons on the actual strict coefficient systems, commuting with finite evaluation, rather than unrelated levelwise choices. The relative dualizing object and a two-sided tensor inverse belong to $D^b_{ctf}(V,\Lambda)$: there is $P\in D^b_{ctf}(V,\Lambda)$ and isomorphisms
$$
 e:\omega_g\otimes^L_\Lambda P\xrightarrow{\sim}\Lambda_V,
 \qquad e':P\otimes^L_\Lambda\omega_g\xrightarrow{\sim}\Lambda_V.
$$
For any inverses $P_d\in D^b_{ctf}(V_d,\Lambda)$ of $\omega_{g_d}$, the inverse $P$ and these two maps may be chosen with components $P_d$ and the specified component inverse maps under the finite-clopen restriction equivalence. The cohomological and Tor intervals can be chosen as common bounds of the finitely many component intervals; integral Tor intervals are uniform in $j$. The empty source, hence the empty family $I$, is included. No Tate orientation is chosen.

proof.text: By [sbc-lem-smooth-relative-dimension-locally-constant], the fibre-dimension function is locally constant. Its level sets $V_d$ are open, and each complement is the union of the other level sets, hence open. They are disjoint and cover $V$. The definition of finite type in [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], applied to the structure map to the affine $\operatorname{Spec}k$, makes $V$ quasi-compact. Thus this open cover has a finite subcover. Disjointness implies that every nonempty level set occurs in that finite subcover, proving finiteness of $I$.

source.place: Tag 02G1, lemma-smooth-omega-finite-locally-free; finite-image consequence of quasi-compactness

proof.text: For each $d\in I$, [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-restrict-open-subschemes](a) gives smoothness of $g_d$. A fibre of $g_d$ is the open subscheme $V_d\cap V_b$ of the corresponding fibre of $g$, so its dimension at a point is unchanged: open neighbourhoods inside that open subset are cofinal among neighbourhoods of the point. Hence its dimension is $d$. By [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-proper](a), $j_d$ is of finite type; apply [lem-sfb-finite-type-composition-base-change](1) to $gj_d$ and to $V_d\to V\to\operatorname{Spec}k$. Thus $g_d$ and $V_d/k$ are of finite type. The diagonal of $g_d$ is the base change of the closed immersion $\Delta_g$ along $V_d\times_BV_d\to V\times_BV$, identifying its inverse image with $V_d$; [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change] proves separatedness. No absolute separatedness of $B$ or $V$ was used.

proof.text: Apply lem-pur-finite-clopen-exceptional-restriction at the finite unit for the finite-coefficient theorem. For the integral and field theorem, apply [lem-pur-finite-clopen-common-exceptional] to choose the identity record R and all component records Ri simultaneously. Their global integral, rational and common-stage functors are equal, while each record retains its normalized strict-system and evaluation comparisons. Evaluating the integral, rational and common-stage comparisons on the coefficient units therefore compares the restriction of the very same global dualizing object to its component exceptional image.

proof.text: The finite theorem uses [lem-pur-smooth-finite-dualizing-inverse] and transports both inverse maps through the finite unit comparison. For the remaining coefficient stages, the proved geometric helper smooth_dimension_on_open_immersion makes each labelled component smooth of pure relative dimension dimension i. Apply [lem-pur-smooth-clopen-component-inverse] to Ri and this pure dimension. It gives inverse pairs for the actual component integralI, rationalI and actionI images of the unit, including integral finite-Tor membership. The proved private helper inverse_pair_transport conjugates these pairs by the corresponding unit comparisons to obtain inverse pairs for the restrictions of the global object; tensor.mapIso supplies both conjugating maps. Integral finite-Tor membership is invariant under these isomorphisms by integralGood_iso, whose proof maps the isomorphism through every scalar reduction and applies the defining Tor test to an isomorphic representative.

source.place: Final invertibility assertion; finite-clopen, orientation-free assembly

proof.text: Apply the proved private categorical helper assemble_dualizing_inverse separately at integral, rational and common-stage coefficients. The restriction equivalences and tensor/unit comparisons are supplied by [lem-pur-finite-clopen-derived-decomposition]. For integral coefficients its finiteTor iff supplies hgood; integralGood_iso supplies invariance under isomorphism. At field coefficients good is top. The helper chooses the inverse image of an arbitrary tuple of prescribed component inverse objects. It lifts both evaluation isomorphisms by full faithfulness; map_preimage and the inverse unit comparison give exactly both specified component equations. It also applies this gluing to the component inverse pairs just obtained, establishing existence of a global inverse. The integral common support and Tor interval assertions are exactly the two interval iff statements of finiteClopen_integral_bounds, with the same a and b and with quantification over all reductions retained. No index is chosen from I, so the same proof handles I empty. The already proved finite theorem uses the corresponding finite bounds and the same categorical gluing helper.

Step 2: smoothness of g_d comes from the open-restriction lemma(a); finite type from the closed-immersion lemma(a) and composition. Separatedness: the diagonal of g_d is the base change of Delta_g, so no absolute separatedness is used. Pure dimension holds because dim_x is unchanged on an open part of a fibre. Step 3: the unit case of lem-pur-finite-clopen-exceptional-restriction; its statement gives the system-level integral coherence. Step 4: the finite-setting hypotheses and thm-asd-smooth-tensor give L[2d]; def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image transports it to the pro-etale site; lem-pur-shifted-line-site-inverse gives both evaluations with Tor intervals [-2d,-2d] and [2d,2d]. At the integral stage the definition gives a derived-complete object with residue nu^*L[2d], which is the hypothesis of the new node with m=2d. Field stages come from rationalizing integral representatives. Step 5: full faithfulness of the finite-clopen equivalence; e_d(a_d x 1) has the right direction; the empty family is covered. Old step 3 cited thm-pur-cohomological-smoothness, which is finite-level under def-pur-conventions; the new route fills that integral gap. New node lem-pur-complete-residue-line-inverse is true. By BS 6.6.8 M is locally a completed perfect C; C tensor k = k[m] forces C = R[m] over a DVR, so M = Line[m]; the dual and evaluations are the rank-one maps. Tested on R^[m], nontrivial monodromy, X empty, and R^/pi (excluded). It is not a restatement and not a duplicate: lem-weil-pbc-/lem-sfb-adic-residue-lisse-perfect-lift give only perfect local models, and lem-pur-integral-line-reduction-restriction starts from a given line.
